focus: correctness — concurrency between two sessions on the packet log

findingDetails.title: Per-packet log lock is scoped to the state directory, so two sessions with different state directories silently lose log rows
findingDetails.evidence: appendGoalLog locks goalScope.stateDir with a packet-scoped name (goal-core.cjs:1050, :894-896) while the directory comes from resolveStateDir (:151-162), which honors OPENCODE_GOAL_STATE_DIR. Divergent directories mean no contention: both writers pass the durable-slice guard (:1069-1073) and the second rename discards the first row. Reproduced with the shipped CLI: same state dir landed both rows; 20 concurrent pairs with state-a/state-b survived 9 x-rows and 11 y-rows, every process reporting STATUS=OK ACTION=log.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Lock acquisition, naming, state-dir resolution, write path and guard read directly; loss reproduced with a same-directory positive control.

focus: correctness — the validator's goal measurement against the runtime extractor

findingDetails.title: Runtime extractor and validator measure different durable slices once a fence carries trailing whitespace
findingDetails.evidence: The runtime fence tolerates trailing whitespace (goal-slice.cjs:24); the validator's goal copy does not (spec-doc-structure.ts:1028), so the frontmatter is measured as part of the durable slice. Observed with both production modules: runtime 3903 characters (warn), validator 4008 (over, SPECDOC_SUFFICIENCY_005), delta exactly the 105-character frontmatter, validator slice containing the fixture secret; exact fences agree. ADR-003's promised golden pin against continuity-freshness.ts:17 does not exist and the vitest fixture writes exact fences only.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both production modules executed on one fixture; the three regexes, the manifest measure and the vitest fixture read directly.

focus: traceability — the speckit YAML packet_goal blocks as executable instructions, and the Devin adapter chain

findingDetails.title: Speckit YAML sanctions a direct table-row append, the one write path the core serializes and guards
findingDetails.evidence: Three command contracts offer 'the goal command's log action or a direct table-row append' (speckit-plan.yaml:195, speckit-implement.yaml:160, speckit-complete.yaml:253). The log action is the only path holding the per-packet lock (goal-core.cjs:1050) and the durable-slice guard (:1069-1073); the OpenCode plugin exposes no log action (opencode-goal.js:168), so on the primary runtime the unsynchronized path is the only one.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Three YAML copies, the lock and guard lines, the plugin action list and the command router read directly.

findingDetails.title: Two Devin UserPromptSubmit hooks write the same additionalContext field and the host merge rule is unrecorded
findingDetails.evidence: .devin/hooks.v1.json registers spec-gate-classify.mjs (:50) and goal-inject.mjs (:55) on one UserPromptSubmit chain; both emit hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (spec-gate-classify.mjs:19-21, goal-inject.mjs:70-74). No test runs both, and the packet records host injection caps as unknown.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both hook commands, both emitters and the adapter header comment read directly.

focus: traceability — plugin versus core parity: workspace resolution and packet-read fields

findingDetails.title: Plugin still resolves a packet against the directory it was handed, so a bind from a subdirectory fails where the core succeeds
findingDetails.evidence: The plugin uses the raw directory (opencode-goal.js:1817-1818), stores it (:1838) and re-resolves against it at render (:2701-2704); the core walks to the repo root (goal-core.cjs:135-144, :191). Reproduced: core bound from scratch/ws/sub and stored the root; the plugin raised PACKET_GOAL_NOT_FOUND on the same input; from the root both agreed. Pass-1 F013 deleted the dead ternary without adding the walk.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both bind paths, the stored pointer and the render resolution read directly; reproduced through the plugin's pinned __test seam and the core on one fixture.

findingDetails.title: Plugin packet action omits the budget field its CLI twin prints
findingDetails.evidence: The plugin's packet block omits packet_budget (opencode-goal.js:2989-2995) while the CLI prints it (bin/goal.cjs:211) and the plugin's own bind reports it (:2974-2977); the shared reader computes budgetState for both (goal-slice.cjs:224-226). Plugin output observed without a budget line.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both packet actions, the bind report and the shared reader read directly; plugin output observed through the test seam.

focus: traceability and completeness — the packet's own fix claims against the shipped code

findingDetails.title: Set-time budget report exists only for a packet bind; a plain-text objective still truncates at 4000 characters with no signal
findingDetails.evidence: The packet log claims the set-time budget report among five fixed P1s (007/goal.md:97) and the summary says each is fixed and pinned by a test (007/implementation-summary.md:58), while ADR-006 still promises a consumer-side check at set time (decision-record.md:559). Only bind reports the tier (bin/goal.cjs:162-167, opencode-goal.js:2974-2977); setGoal truncates through sanitizeInlineText and clampText with no signal (goal-core.cjs:1114-1121, :236-243). Reproduced: a 5000-character objective stored as exactly 4000 characters ending in '...' with STATUS=OK and no warning field.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Packet log, summary, ADR decision, both set implementations, both bind reports and clampText read directly; truncation reproduced end to end.

results.summary: ADR-003's one-extractor claim is unmet: the runtime and the validator measure different durable slices on a tolerant fence, and the promised golden pin does not exist.
Every task is checked and the evidence table exists; two claimed fixes are incomplete or unpinned.
The target is a spec folder, not a skill-agent pair.
Pi, Cursor and Devin inherit the core's repo-root walk; the OpenCode plugin does not, and its packet read omits the budget field the CLI prints.
Changelog and the 009 requirement row agree with the shipped Devin adapter and the packet-bound model.
The command contracts instruct an append path the core serializes only when the log action is used.
